A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICM research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support matching retained, relocated, revised, and added content.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification accuracies, noise measurements, gradient analyses, and ablations across synthetic and human-annotated complementary-label datasets, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and reports additional encoder comparisons, architecture analyses, and repeated-run significance analyses.

M1.justification: ICM retains SimSiam embeddings, k-means clustering, within-cluster pair mixing, and the same mixed loss. MICM's three-sample Dirichlet mixing and inverse-distance label weighting already appear in v1 Appendix C. Simplified coefficient notation and revised indexing do not change these procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, KMNIST, FMNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR20, CLCIFAR10, and CLCIFAR20. Balanced learning and the three imbalance constructions in Appendix B are retained. The added analyses vary models and encoders within existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 5 adds MoCov3 and BYOL as evaluated encoder alternatives to the SimSiam-based ICM configuration. The principal comparisons involving SCL-NL, SCL-EXP, FWD-INT, DM, and original Mixup remain unchanged; the comparator expansion is confined to the encoder ablation.

E3.justification: V2 adds an encoder-comparison protocol using ResNet18 encoders trained on CIFAR10 for 800 epochs and an explicit architecture comparison on imbalanced MNIST with ratio 100 (Appendices D.6–D.7). The main 300-epoch, batch-size-512 Adam training protocol remains unchanged. These additions do not establish that the original benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands sensitivity analysis: Figures 6 and 11 examine architectural capacity, while Table 5 and Appendix D.7 test encoder choice through both accuracy and induced noise. These directly probe important dependencies of ICM. Existing augmentation, label-sharing, gradient, MICM, and hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 reports three runs and mean/standard-deviation results. V2 retains those table values but adds a separate five-run statistical-validation study, boxplots, and p-values across CIFAR10, CLCIFAR10, and MNIST (Appendix D.5; Figures 4 and 13–15). This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, although the significance test is not identified.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark table values remain unchanged, but substantial additional outcomes are reported. V2 Table 5 gives ICM accuracies of 79.13%, 60.45%, and 61.47% with SimSiam, MoCov3, and BYOL, respectively. Architecture results establish gains on MNIST/KMNIST for simpler models, revising v1's broad deterioration statement. Five-run distributions and p-values are added, and plotted values change in v1 Figure 7 versus v2 Figure 9.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 introduces same-cluster pairing into Definition 1 and explicitly relates local and aggregate noise errors. Appendix A replaces the existing proof with a zero-one-loss indicator derivation. This is a substantive revision of one existing argument, although the rewritten proof inconsistently subtracts and then adds noise terms and does not establish a corrected guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: ordinary Mixup introduces harmful complementary-label noise, and within-cluster mixing improves CLL across synthetic, real-world, balanced, and imbalanced settings. MICM's increased visibility in the main text does not introduce a new contribution.

C2.justification: V2 identifies encoder sensitivity, proposes excessive input distortion as an explanation for Cutout's poorer combination with ICM, and narrows the simpler-model limitation from the MNIST family generally to FMNIST. These refine applicability and mechanism interpretations without replacing the central label-noise explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix D.7 newly documents CIFAR10, ResNet18, and 800-epoch pretraining for MoCov3 and BYOL, with hyperparameters shared with SimSiam. Existing classifier settings, hardware, and hyperparameter selections remain. Neither PDF supplies a new access route to this work's code or data.

R1.justification: V2 adds references covering alternative complementary-label generation, ConMix, GraphMAD, Global Mixup, alternative self-supervised encoders, and libcll. These modestly broaden the background and support the added analyses; the claimed novelty of applying tailored Mixup augmentation to CLL remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of definitions, the proof, and experimental discussion. The surrogate-loss subsection becomes an unnumbered part of Section 3.2, Appendices D.5–D.7 are added, and publication information and acknowledgements appear. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds four significance-plot figures, two architecture figures, and an encoder table. Figure 3 gains an accuracy panel, MICM plots are redrawn, and the framework and initial diagnostic figures exchange order. Tables receive shaded emphasis and subscript dispersion values. Together these substantially revise the visual presentation beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The encoder and architecture analyses better establish where ICM succeeds or fails and correct v1's overly broad simpler-model limitation. Five-run distributions add empirical support while the main benchmark results remain intact. The overall gain is limited: the significance test is unspecified, and the rewritten Appendix A proof still fails to justify its noise decomposition.
